Q1_ensemble.question: Does pooling all testers' incomplete-source suites match one tester's complete-source suites?
Q1_ensemble.unit: requirement, equal weight; detection = share of confirmed mutants killed by >=1 sound suite

Q2_agreement.caveat: Mutants of one requirement are not independent; the pooled comparison is descriptive.
Q2_agreement.question: Do testers miss the same confirmed losses?
Q2_agreement.unit: confirmed mutant (pooled across requirements); independence uses each tester's marginal rate

Q3_coupling.caveat: Eligibility requires at least one confirmed mutant, so fully recovered rules are absent: the range of generator recovery is truncated.

escape.note: loss = 1 - generator recovery; miss = 1 - incomplete-source detection; per requirement, equal weight; truncated to requirements with >=1 confirmed mutant

Q3_coupling.question: Are rules the generators recover also the ones testers notice from the incomplete request?
Q3_coupling.unit: requirement; generator recovery = recovered / (recovered + confirmed mutants) in arm C of the 46-case collection, restricted to these 25 eligible requirements (each has >=1 mutant by construction)

Q4_anchoring.difference: alarm(recovered) - alarm(mutant); positive = the suite rewards the loss
Q4_anchoring.question: Within arm C, do suites alarm more on implementations that kept the rule than on those that lost it?
Q4_anchoring.unit: requirement with >=1 recovered and >=1 mutant; sound suites; code_incomplete excludes the mutant whose code the tester saw

Q5_soundness.note: A suite that alarms on the reference is unsound and cannot kill any mutant under the published rule.
Q5_soundness.question: How often does a suite reject the correct reference implementation?
